title: Worker HTTP API
description: Request and response bodies for the Worker's HTTP routes. Every error response body is common.json ErrorBody. The Worker validates, authenticates, then calls the pod Durable Object; all authorization lives in the pod, never the client.

x-routes.protocol: 302 to GitHub's authorize page, with a same-origin path in ?next; sets the one-use state cookie
302 to the next path bound to the state; sets the session cookie
mcp-streamable-http, stateless; the MCP adapter over operations.json

x-rules: /__test/* routes exist only when ENV is local or preview, and are absent from the production bundle.

A device code polled before approval gets authorization_pending; once refused, access_denied on every poll; after approval exactly one exchange succeeds and the next gets invalid_grant; an expired code gets expired_token; a poll sooner than interval after the last one gets slow_down.

Jellymoon mints the device code itself; GitHub only proves who the person is, through its OAuth web flow at /v1/auth/github/*. The GitHub token is dropped after GET /user: never stored, logged or returned. A GitHub 401 there gets unauthorized; any other GitHub failure gets upstream.

The callback is refused (forbidden) when its state is missing, differs from the state cookie, or was already used: a state is good for one callback, and the next path it carries is the one bound at start. A next that is not a same-origin path (one leading /, not // or /\, no scheme) becomes /.

The session cookie (httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure except ENV=local) is accepted, besides a Bearer jmu_, by every route whose auth includes user, the pod WebSocket included, and by every user operation. A request with a Bearer uses it and ignores the cookie. The cookie must hold a jmu_: any other token in it is no caller (unauthorized). Routes and operations whose auth is only run or computer, and POST /mcp, read the Bearer alone.

A cookie-authenticated request that changes state (any method but GET, HEAD and OPTIONS) needs Content-Type application/json and an Origin header equal to the server's own origin (PUBLIC_URL, or the request's origin, https except ENV=local); a missing Origin is refused too (forbidden). The pod WebSocket opened by the cookie needs the same Origin. A token never rides in the query string. Bearer requests need neither. POST /v1/auth/device/approve and POST /v1/auth/device/deny are cookie writes like any other.

POST /v1/auth/logout (cookie or Bearer jmu_) revokes the token the request presented, at once, and clears the session cookie. A request with both a Bearer jmu_ and the session cookie revokes both tokens. Every pod WebSocket opened with a revoked token is closed.
A user token (jmu_) stops authenticating at its expiresAt, 30 days after it was issued: unauthorized on every route and on the pod WebSocket, as a Bearer and as the session cookie.

POST /v1/auth/device and GET /v1/auth/github/start each take a fixed number of requests per client address per minute. Past it they get rate_limited (HTTP 429) with a Retry-After header: the whole seconds until the minute ends.
An expired device code or OAuth state is deleted an hour after it expires; a deleted device code gets invalid_grant. A call to GitHub that takes over 10 seconds gets upstream.

POST /v1/auth/device/approve needs Content-Type application/json, and by the session cookie the server's own Origin, which a missing Origin is not (forbidden). The user code matches in either case, with or without its hyphen. An unknown user code gets not_found, an expired one expired_token, an approved or refused one gone. It is the only route that approves a device code.

POST /v1/auth/device/approve and POST /v1/auth/device/deny share one guess limit (RFC 8628 section 5.1), checked before the code is looked up. A signed-in person gets 10 failed lookups (an unknown, expired or used code) per fixed ten minutes across both routes; past them every approve and deny from that person, a valid code included, gets rate_limited (HTTP 429) with a Retry-After header: the whole seconds until the ten minutes end. Each failed lookup also counts in POST /v1/auth/device's limit for the client address, so accounts from one address share that limit, and past it approve, deny and the start get rate_limited with Retry-After until the minute ends. A successful approve or deny counts in neither.

POST /v1/auth/device/deny refuses a device code its caller did not start: a signed-in person, with approve's auth, Content-Type, Origin and user-code matching, and approve's guess limit. It acts only on a pending, unexpired code and is idempotent: refusing a refused code is a success again. Every refusal of it is approve's answer for the same code, byte for byte (unknown not_found, expired expired_token, approved or exchanged gone), so it tells a guesser nothing approve does not. A refused code cannot be approved (gone), and its poll gets access_denied.
A used or expired invite gets gone (HTTP 410). Only a member can create an invite.
GET /v1/invites/:code needs no sign-in and changes nothing: it never uses or extends the invite. An unknown, used or expired code gets the same not_found body, so a guesser learns nothing more.
GET /v1/invites/:code, like the accept, has no rate limit: a code is inv_ and 22 base62 characters, too many to guess.
GET /v1/session is GET /v1/me that never refuses: 200 with the user for a live Bearer jmu_ or session cookie, and 200 with no user otherwise. GET /v1/me still answers unauthorized to nobody.
cancelled is final. A later POST /v1/runs/:run/end for a run a person stopped is accepted and does not change the outcome.
Only a pod owner connects a vendor or grants an agent access; a member gets forbidden.

A connect lists the upstream's operations and compares them with the vendor's pinned catalogue. An empty list, or a pinned operation missing upstream or with other argument names, refuses the connect with connector_drift; an upstream that fails the listing gets upstream_failed with its error.

The url is https and carries no credentials. Its host, and every address its name resolves to, must be outside the loopback, private, link-local and reserved ranges; this is checked again before every upstream request, and each request is pinned to the checked address. ENV=local allows only a literal loopback address, over http or https.
The token is stored only as an AES-256-GCM envelope under the server's vault key and is never returned. Without JM_VAULT_KEY a connect or a connector call gets vault_unconfigured.
A grant names an agent registered in the pod (otherwise not_found) and an access. A second grant to the same agent on the same connection replaces the first.
Only a pod owner sets a connection's approver set (a member gets forbidden). Each userId must be a pod member (otherwise not_found). The set replaces the last one; an empty list clears it.

A ruling on a connector write's ask is allowed for a pod owner or a member on that connection's approver set at the time of the ruling, and refused forbidden for anyone else, a removed approver included.

DeviceStartResponse.description: The answer to starting a device sign-in: the code the client exchanges for a token and the code the person types.

deviceCode.description: The code the client exchanges for a token.

userCode.description: What the person types on the sign-in page, e.g. WDJB-MJHT.

verificationUri.description: The page where the person enters the user code. https only.

DeviceTokenRequest.description: Exchanges a device code for a user token once the person has approved it.

deviceCode.description: The deviceCode from the sign-in start.

DeviceApproveRequest.description: A signed-in person approves the device code they were shown, binding it to themselves.

userCode.description: The code the sign-in page shows, e.g. WDJB-MJHT, in either case and with or without the hyphen.

DeviceDenyRequest.description: A signed-in person refuses a device code they did not start, so the device polling it gets access_denied.

userCode.description: The code the sign-in page shows, e.g. WDJB-MJHT, in either case and with or without the hyphen.

DeviceDenyResponse.description: A refusal carries no data: the device that polls gets access_denied.

LogoutResponse.description: A logout carries no data: the token it presented no longer authenticates, and the session cookie is cleared.

DeviceApproveResponse.description: An approval carries no data: the device that polls gets the token.

DeviceTokenResponse.description: A user token and the user it belongs to.

Pod.description: A pod: its id, name and creation time.

CreateInviteRequest.description: Options for a new invite. Both fields have defaults.

Invite.description: An invite to a pod: its code and link, when it expires and how many uses are left.

code.description: The code a person gives to accept the invite.

url.description: The link to share. https only.

usesLeft.description: How many more times the invite can be accepted.

InvitePreview.description: What an invite page shows before anyone signs in: the pod's name, who invited you and when the invite expires. No ids, no email, no members.

inviterName.description: The display name of the member who created the invite.

SessionResponse.description: Who the request is signed in as. user is absent when nobody is: no token, or a dead one.

RegisterComputerResponse.description: The new computer's id and its computer token.

RegisterAgentRequest.description: A computer registers an agent in a pod.

ClaimRunRequest.description: The daemon claims a run for a wake.

ClaimRunResponse.description: The brief is built by the server and sent as the agent's first prompt. The run token goes to the agent; the computer token never does.

brief.description: The agent's first prompt, built by the server.

mcpUrl.description: Where the agent reaches the pod's MCP server. https, or http on localhost or 127.0.0.1. The daemon must check scheme and host itself before sending the run token: Go does not enforce patterns.

ConnectRequest.description: A pod owner connects an upstream: the vendor, where its operations are served, and the credential the pod will hold.

url.description: The upstream's endpoint, e.g. its remote MCP URL. https only (http on loopback when ENV is local).

token.description: The upstream credential. Stored encrypted and never shown again, to anyone.

Connection.description: A stored connection, without its credential: the vendor, the url and the pinned operations the upstream was checked against.

operations.description: The pinned catalogue the upstream matched.

GrantRequest.description: A pod owner lets one agent use one connection, read only or with writes that each need approval.

Grant.description: A stored grant: which agent may use which connection, how, and since when.

ApproversRequest.description: A pod owner names the members, besides the pod owners, who may approve this connection's writes. An empty list clears the set.

userIds.description: The approvers, each a member of the pod. A repeat is refused with invalid_input.

Approvers.description: A connection's approver set as stored: the members who may approve its writes besides the pod owners.

userIds.description: The approvers, in the order they were named.

RunOutcome.description: How a run ended: completed, failed or cancelled.

EndRunRequest.description: The daemon reports that a run ended.

harnessVersion.description: The harness version, as the daemon reports it.
